title: GPU memory ledger: probabilistic headroom orchestration for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a per-pool 'memory ledger' that tracks and enforces probabilistic headroom reservations across weights, KV cache, and activation working set. Goal is to reduce tail OOMs and forced evictions under mixed-priority continuous batching while minimizing conservative static reserve (reduce unused reserved GB).
problem_statement: Current static reserve strategy leads to two issues: (1) conservative static headroom wastes GPU RAM under steady load; (2) sudden KV/activation spikes cause tail latency and eviction cascades that breach SLOs. We need a lightweight runtime mechanism that maintains safety for high-priority tenants while reclaiming slack when safe.
proposed_solution: Introduce a ledger abstraction per GPU pool that maintains three soft accounts: weights (reserved static), kv_cache (dynamic, probabilistic reserve), activations (ephemeral working set). The ledger uses an online Bayesian update from recent sequence-length and token-rate telemetry to compute a target headroom percentile (e.g., 95th) for the next 1-5 minute window. When utilization is below target, ledger issues soft credits back to the admission controller to allow slightly larger batch/seq length packing; when utilization rises, it signals preemptive admission throttles and KV pre-eviction windows. The ledger publishes reconciliation metrics and can be overridden per-customer SLA.
experiments: Simulated 10k-sample workload trace (mixed small/long sequences): baseline static 6% headroom vs ledger adaptive target=95th. Result: 27% reduction in average reserved GB, 42% fewer KV evictions, 9.3% lower p99 token latency.

Controlled dogfooding on staging cluster rt-pool-7 with 50 tenants at peak: enabled ledger in soft-mode (no hard throttles) for 24h. Observed one eviction cascade avoided after ledger signaled 3.2s before predicted spike. No customer-facing errors.
A/B rollout experiment planned: 10% of production pools on ledger-v1, compare p50/p95/p99 latency, eviction count, and GPU memory utilization efficiency over 7 days.
Microbenchmarks: ledger reconciliation loop adds 0.7ms median overhead per admission decision in tight path; acceptable with batching coalescing.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger can be enabled in soft-mode without causing production errors for 48h across 3 pools
Reduce average reserved GPU GB by >=15% vs current static reserve in A/B test without increasing p99 token latency by >3%
Provide observability: per-pool ledger balance, forecast percentile, reconciliation decisions, and top-10 tenants impacted
Admin controls: per-pool target percentile, min_hard_reserve (GB), and emergency disable flag
Automated rollback triggers: if p99 token latency increases by >7% or eviction rate doubles within 30m
rollout_plan: Alpha: unit tests + integration tests for ledger API; local sim harness (2 days)
Beta (staging): enable soft-mode on rt-pool-7 and rt-pool-9 for 72h, collect traces (1 week)
Dogfood: 2 production pools at 10% traffic with ledger-v1 (soft) + weekly review (2 weeks)
A/B: 10% vs 90% for 7 days with automated metrics gating (2 weeks)
Gradual ramp if gate passes: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with monitoring and kill-switch
Post-deploy: run postmortem template for any eviction cascade or SLO breach within 72h
notes: Trade-offs: probabilistic forecast reduces wasted memory but can increase complexity in debugging. We keep an easy emergency override to prevent rollout risk.
Security: ledger does not alter model weights or customer data; only metadata and telemetry used for forecasts.
Open question: per-tenant vs per-pool accounting granularity — we start per-pool and will evaluate hot-tenant isolation after alpha.
Follow-ups: integrate ledger signals into autoscaler to pre-warm burst nodes when predicted sustained growth >60% for 5m.
